problem: "The same system can be written K/(s + a) with a = 1/τ" is not equal to K/(1 + τs). Dividing the denominator by τ also divides the numerator by τ, so the constant in front changes. As written, a student will copy a form that gives the wrong gain.
fix: Write: K/(1 + τs) = (K/τ)/(s + 1/τ). Here a = 1/τ and the numerator becomes K/τ, not K. The DC gain is still K; only after re-labelling the numerator as K′ = K/τ does the form K′/(s + a) hold.

problem: "The exact 2% settling time is 4τ" is a wrong number stated as exact. At 4τ the output is 98.2% of final, an error of 1.8%, which is inside the 2% band; the exact 2% time is τ ln 50 ≈ 3.9τ, not 4τ.
fix: At 5τ the output is 99.3% of final, so the remaining error is 0.674%. The exact 1% settling time is τ ln 100 ≈ 4.605τ; the exact 2% time is τ ln 50 ≈ 3.91τ, which engineers round to 4τ by convention. 5τ is a convenient rule of thumb, not a definition.

problem: "So τ is a time delay, not a vertical offset in seconds" mixes two different quantities. A delay has units of seconds; a vertical offset has units of output. The sentence as written is easy to misread.
fix: So τ appears as a time delay of τ seconds along the time axis; the vertical gap between the scaled input Kt and the steady ramp response K(t − τ) is Kτ, in output units.

problem: Several exponents are written without a superscript, for example "c₀e−t/τ", "10(1 − e−t/2)", "4e−2t". On a phone screen these read as e minus t over τ, not e to the power minus t over τ.
fix: Use the superscript tag everywhere the exponential appears: c₀e<sup>−t/τ</sup>, 10(1 − e<sup>−t/2</sup>), 4e<sup>−2t</sup>, τ²(1 − e<sup>−t/τ</sup>).

problem: "Some syllabi call the step curve the transient response" is loose. Transient response means the whole time-varying part of any response (step, ramp or impulse), not the step curve only. A student may take the two as synonyms.
fix: Some syllabi call the time-varying part of the response the transient part, and the exponential curve e<sup>−t/τ</sup> that sets its shape the exponential mode of the system.
